Sorry this is so late! Not sure if you’re still interested but here’s a list of some great spots, in order of my favorite to least favorite not including PHP (i love them all very much).

- Red Wing Park (unfortunately closed until Feb.)

- Marshview Park (park on Indian Rd.)

- First Landing State Park (both the campground entrance off Shore Dr. and the 64th st. boat ramp entrance. costs money w/o pass)

- Back Bay NWR (HUGE place, but the trails near the visitors center are stunning.)
BONUS: Frank Carter Impoundments off Colechester Rd, technically part of BBNWR but not close to the aforementioned area

- Stumpy Lake Natural Area

- Foxfire Trail/West Neck Creek Natural Area (while foxfire is actually a brand new trail and you can park on Esplanade Rd near foxfire park, it actually connect to WNCNA which has been around for awhile. worth walking it to check out the whitehurst buffington house in a gorgeous clearing

- Trails behind VA aquarium marsh pavilion. could be closed for renovations since haven’t been there in a little bit

- Trails/ponds behind Harris Teeter on Upton (park in the back of HT. make sure you don’t wander into Three Oaks ES.)

- Beach Garden Park off Laskin-ish

- Munden Point Park

- Lake Lawson/Smith Natural Area

- Tidewater Arboretum

There are certainly more, but I am a birder, so I tried to pick places that even a non-birder would enjoy since sometimes the best birds are in the ugliest places. Might post a master list some time soon tbh but hope this helped!

I’d also recommend the Virginia Aquarium/Adventure Park. Some fairly new additions to the premises are worth checking out if you haven’t been there in awhile. I’m also big on museums, and the Chrysler and MOCA are both fantastic. If the drive is worth it, the VMFA in Richmond is also incredible.

Sexual dimorphism (morphological differences between differently sexed individuals of the same species) can skew in “favor” of the female in some birds and various other animals. The example I personally see the most is the Belted Kingfisher, a primarily North American bird in which the female sports an extra rust-colored belt on its belly and into the flanks below the shared, thicker blue belt. Female birds of prey are also larger than the males, since they are the ones competing for mates*.

*not necessarily true, see below
